transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-04 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah, Marco Diaz, Evelyn Cho (Redwood); Jordan Miles, Sana Patel, Dr. Rahul Nair, Maya Lin (Cedarpark)

Summary: quick kickoff to align Cedarpark onboarding path; customer leaning toward a Private/VPC eval with potential Dedicated commit depending on latencies and security. Lots of questions on SSO and KMS, plus a request for a hands-on infra workshop.

[00:00] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have a packed 50 minutes, so we'll go through roles, objectives, then network and security, and finish with concrete next steps. Jordan, can you confirm the main success criteria for this pilot?

[00:18] Jordan Miles: Yeah, sure. Thanks Priya. High level: we want to validate that Redwood can meet sub-200ms median latency for our call patterns, keep costs under our projected threshold, and ensure data never leaves our VPC for PHI workflows. So basically latency, cost, and data residency.

[00:39] Evelyn Cho: Got it. When you say 'our call patterns' — can you give a sense of sequence lengths and concurrency? That helps a lot for kernel selection and batching settings.

[00:48] Jordan Miles: Most calls are short — 40 to 120 tokens, but we'll have infrequent longer sessions for note generation — up to 1k tokens. Concurrency won't exceed 30 qps in pilot, maybe burst to 80 for testing.

[01:12] Sana Patel: And to underline, any PHI must remain within our environment — we can't allow logging to external storage. So private deployment with customer-managed KMS is preferred.

[01:26] Marco Diaz: Totally understood, that's why we'll outline Private options. For context, we usually recommend Private (VPC) for PHI; Dedicated for teams who want isolation but are ok with Redwood-managed infra. Priya, do you want to say a quick bit about the Private package?

[01:40] Priya Shah: Sure — Redwood Private gives you a customer-controlled VPC peering option to our control plane, optional air-gapped on-prem bundle if needed, and KMS integrations for key management. We keep audit logs but we can route them to your logging endpoint so nothing persists on our side if that's required.

[01:58] Maya Lin: When you say route logs — are those event logs or full request/response bodies? We can't have request bodies with PHI.

[02:06] Priya Shah: Good callout. By default audit logs are event metadata only (timestamps, model invoked, token counts, error codes). We do have optional request/response logging for debugging but that's explicitly opt-in and can be disabled for PHI workloads. We'll include that detail in the security pack.

[02:23] Dr. Rahul Nair: How about SAML — we run Okta and want RBAC tied to our Okta groups. Is that supported out of the box or a custom effort?

[02:33] Evelyn Cho: We support SAML/SAML2 and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC can be mapped to groups from your IdP; there can be a short config step in the console and some metadata exchange. For Private installs it's the same flow but often the SP metadata is hosted internally, so we'll need your SAML metadata and service account details.

[02:54] Sana Patel: Cool. We'll need to know what attributes you need in the assertion. Also, does Redwood enforce session timeouts and MFA requirements proxied from Okta?

[03:06] Evelyn Cho: We respect the assertions from your IdP. Session TTLs can be set on our side too, but MFA enforcement is IdP-level — we don't replace that. We'll document recommended settings.

[03:18] Jordan Miles: Network question — you mentioned VPC peering and private link. We use AWS in us-west-2. What is the recommended pattern?

[03:27] Priya Shah: For us-west-2, VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink are both viable. PrivateLink reduces exposure and is preferred for cross-account service endpoints. With peering we can do CIDR restrictions and route table controls. We'll surface network diagrams in the pack.

[03:43] Maya Lin: Any ports or CIDR ranges we should pre-approve? Our security team hates surprises.

[03:49] Evelyn Cho: We'll include an exact list — generally outbound TLS to our control plane, plus peered subnets for the runtime. No open inbound to your public internet.

[03:58] Jordan Miles: Can we run an early smoke test with a tiny footprint to validate latency before committing to a bigger environment?

[04:06] Marco Diaz: Absolutely — we recommend a two-week pilot: start small (2 GPU nodes), run defined traffic patterns, then scale if metrics look good. We'll provide a test harness and a sample workload script.

[04:20] Jordan Miles: Great. Who on Redwood will run the infra workshop? We want hands-on and a checklist we can walk through with Sana.

[04:27] Evelyn Cho: That would be me. I will lead the infra runbook workshop — we'll walk through VPC peering, IAM roles, SAML metadata exchange, KMS envelope keys, and a basic benchmarking run. I'll send a prep doc and a checklist.

[04:42] Sana Patel: On KMS — we use AWS KMS with an external key policy. Can Redwood accept CMKs and perform envelope encryption?

[04:51] Evelyn Cho: Yes, envelope encryption with customer-managed CMKs is supported. For Private we can configure the key policy to allow our runtime principal to use the key, but you retain ownership and rotation control. We'll need the key ARN and a short key policy snippet.

[05:05] Maya Lin: Any compliance artifacts you can share now? SOC 2, ISO? Also penetration test cadence?

[05:12] Priya Shah: We'll send a security pack with SOC 2 Type II summary, ISO section highlights, recent pen test report extract, and our data flow diagrams. The pack will also include our expected SLAs for Dedicated/Private.

[05:25] Jordan Miles: Perfect. About cost — we need estimates for the pilot and then modeled run rates at 100 qps. Can you give a sense now or should we wait for Marco's pricing note?

[05:35] Marco Diaz: I'll draft both pilot and steady-state estimates. There's a trade-off between Dedicated and Private: Dedicated gives predictable committed pricing, whereas Private may have higher baseline infra costs but better data controls. I'll include example numbers and a comparison matrix.

[05:52] Dr. Rahul Nair: For the benchmark, what metrics will you capture? Token latency, tail percentiles?

[05:58] Evelyn Cho: We'll capture median and p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rates, and throughput at target seq lengths. Also KV cache hit rates if you decide to enable prefix caching. Note: sometimes the transcript engine transcribes KV cache as K V cash in logs — ha.

[06:18] (laughter)

[06:23] Sana Patel: (laugh) noted. One more: do you support model pinning and automatic fallback to smaller models if capacity spikes? We need predictable degradation.

[06:33] Priya Shah: Yes — Redwood supports model pinning and routing policies with automatic fallback to compatible variants. You can set SLOs to prefer latency or cost and configure fallback order. We'll show examples in the runbook.

[06:48] Jordan Miles: Ok timing: we'd like to start the infra workshop next week, then run a 2-week pilot starting 6/15. Is that feasible?

[06:56] Evelyn Cho: Week of 6/8 works for the workshop; starting pilot week of 6/15 is realistic. We'll need your test credentials and datasets by 6/9 to provision and do prechecks.

[07:07] Marco Diaz: I'll also create a pilot success template for KPIs — Jordan, we can iterate on that quickly.

[07:12] Jordan Miles: I'll add a few user stories now.

[07:17] Priya Shah: Quick recap before we close — actions: security pack to Cedarpark by 6/7 (Priya), pricing and pilot comparison by 6/8 (Marco), infra workshop invite + checklist by 6/8 (Evelyn), Cedarpark to provide test data and SAML metadata by 6/9 (Sana). Anything else?

[07:35] Maya Lin: Please include contact for escalation and a runbook link for incident response.

[07:40] Priya Shah: Yes, we'll include escalation path and our on-call rotation.

[07:45] Jordan Miles: Sounds good to me. Thanks all.

[07:49] Priya Shah: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.

End of meeting.
